summary: Best fit for Neo4j-style graph exploration: MIT, zero dependencies, SLSA provenance, active, 15.8M weekly downloads, 138 KB gzip. Layouts come via extensions; the React wrapper is stale, so use the core API with a ref or a thin internal wrapper.
reasoning: MIT with a public repository and SLSA provenance from .github/workflows/release.yml.
Zero runtime dependencies; 6 MB install and 138 KB gzip for the core bundle.
Layouts are extensions (dagre, cose-bilkent, fcose), so the feature set matches the NVL layouts without the proprietary licence.
Canvas renderer handles typical Neo4j result sizes; for very large graphs, Sigma is the fallback.
caveats: react-cytoscapejs is stale (last release 2022, 45 open issues, no types). Use cytoscape directly with a ref, or maintain a thin wrapper.
Layout extensions are separate packages with their own maintenance and licences.
Canvas rendering is slower than WebGL above roughly 10k-20k visible nodes.
The package ships UMD/ESM/CJS bundles, so the unpacked size is larger than the bundled cost.
